problem: End-to-end VLN agents with unstructured recurrent memory (LSTM/GRU) work in the nav-graph teleport setting but degrade sharply when the agent must move freely with low-level actions (VLN-CE). Learning mapping, planning and control jointly end-to-end is also data-hungry and fragile without GT odometry.
motivation: Robotics and visual-navigation work shows that modular pipelines with structured memory (metric or topological maps) are robust and interpretable, but these had not been studied for VLN. The authors observe that predicting a path in a discrete topological map is analogous to autoregressive sequence prediction in language modeling and NMT. That lets transformer cross-modal attention relate instruction words such as 'bedroom' to places in the map.
key_idea: Build a panoramic topological map from pre-exploration. Plan a node path autoregressively with a GNN plus an LXMERT-style cross-modal transformer conditioned on the instruction. Execute the plan with a separately trained, localization-aware waypoint controller that outputs FORWARD/ROTATE actions.
insight: Decoupling planning from control shows where the difficulty lies. The controller alone reaches high success (82.5–92.6% on multi-node plans in unseen environments, Table 2), and the integrated controller success CS is 83–93%, so the bottleneck is the planner and in particular its stop decision. The no-stop ablation CMTP-NS reaches 64.0 oracle success on AG val-unseen, while CMTP's SR is 26.0 (planner-only, Table 1): the planner usually visits the right place but fails to stop there. Other findings: map quality matters, since pre-defined R2R graphs beat agent-generated maps (e.g. 28.9 vs 25.3 best unseen SR). The Gaussian 'stubbornness' bias against perceptual-aliasing oscillation raises controller success on AG unseen from 82.5 (unbiased) to 89.6 (σ²=3), but too strong a bias hurts (σ²=2: 75.9). Autoregressive transformer planning beats a GNN that predicts only the goal node (SR 23.1 vs 22.1 unseen AG, 30.5 vs 26.3 SPL seen AG).
method: Topological map from pre-exploration: 10 pre-defined exploration trajectories per scene (waypoints sampled from the GT traversability map). Each dense trajectory is sparsified with an oracle reachability estimator (line-of-sight and d_sp=4m, after Meng et al.), then the per-trajectory maps are merged and nodes within 2m are fused (p_merge=0.5). Nodes are 360° RGB-D panoramas in a fixed global orientation.
Edge geometry: each directed edge gets a learned embedding of a quantized polar category (8 directions × 3 distance bins: 0-2m, 2-5m, >5m), computed with GT odometry at map-construction time.

GNN map encoder: 6 Graph-Network blocks (Battaglia et al.) with 4-layer MLP update functions and sum aggregation. Node inputs are ResNet152 panorama features, edges are category embeddings; the output is 768-d node features that encode appearance and connectivity.

Cross-modal transformer planner (CMTP): LXMERT-style, trained from scratch, with 9 language layers, 5 map layers and 5 cross-modal layers. Map tokens get learned trajectory positional embeddings (a shared E_NT embedding for non-trajectory nodes). It predicts the next plan node autoregressively by classifying over nodes plus a [STOP] token, trained with cross-entropy and AdamW. Stop-mechanism variants: CMTP-BCE (separate binary stop loss) and CMTP-R (stop by repeating a node).

High-level controller C_high: a circular-convolution encoder over the triplet of aligned RGB-D panoramas (previous subgoal, current view, current subgoal), plus embedding differences. It predicts the waypoint direction (24 sectors of 15°) and a distance ρ. Trained offline on 2M synthetic samples plus DAgger against A* expert waypoints at a fixed lookahead; ρ≤d is used to localize and consume the subgoal.

Oscillation handling and low-level control: direction probabilities are reweighted by a Gaussian centred on the previous argmax ('stubbornness', variance σ²). C_low rotates 15° toward the chosen sector or moves FORWARD 0.25m once it faces it.

setting.backbone: ResNet152 panorama features + 6-block GNN + LXMERT-style cross-modal transformer (trained from scratch, no pre-training) for planning; circular-conv CNN waypoint controller trained with imitation/DAgger
setting.training_data: VLN-CE (R2R) train episodes converted into node paths on agent-generated maps or R2R nav graphs (episodes with start/goal >2m from any node discarded). Controller: 2 million synthetic (o_prev, o_curr, o_subgoal)→waypoint samples from A* expert waypoints, plus DAgger. No external or web data.
setting.observation: 360° panoramic RGB-D + ground-truth heading (no position at test time); stored panoramas of the pre-built topological map nodes
setting.action_space: low-level FORWARD 0.25 m / ROTATE left/right 15° (via predicted waypoint subgoals along a planned topological node path)
setting.privileged: Pre-exploration: 10 pre-defined exploration trajectories per environment, with waypoints sampled from GT metric/traversability maps, used to build the topological map before any episode. GT odometry is used to label map edges and an oracle reachability estimator (GT traversability) is used for sparsification. GT heading is available at test time. The R2R-graph variants use the pre-defined R2R navigation graphs as the map.

numbers_note: Integrated-system numbers (Table 3) are recorded here. Table 1 (planner-only SR/OS/NE on AG and R2R graphs, including the CMTP-NS no-stop ablation) and Table 2 (controller-only success with a 1m threshold for point goals and random plans under different bias σ²) are separate component evaluations and are not included. Evaluation runs in iGibson, not Habitat, on VLN-CE episodes filtered by distance to the map (>2m discarded), and the number of remaining episodes is not reported. The filtered subset may differ between AG and R2R maps. The VLN-CE baseline (SR 19.7 / SPL 14.1 unseen) was retrained by the authors in iGibson, so the numbers are not directly comparable to standard Habitat VLN-CE leaderboards.
results: On VLN-CE episodes in iGibson, the modular topological-map system beats the end-to-end VLN-CE cross-modal baseline retrained in iGibson (SR 22.2 seen / 19.7 unseen, SPL 16.5 / 14.1). CMTP on agent-generated maps reaches 35.9/23.1 SR and 30.5/19.1 SPL, and CMTP-R reaches 36.3/25.3 SR. The best unseen result is CMTP-BCE on pre-defined R2R graphs (28.9 SR, 24.1 SPL). Transformer planners also beat a GNN goal-prediction baseline, and the controller executes about 83–93% of plans. The authors note that part of the gain over VLN-CE comes from pre-exploration.
limitations: Relies on pre-exploration with trajectories generated from GT metric maps, GT odometry for edge labels and an oracle reachability estimator; the map is not built at test time. The comparison to end-to-end VLN-CE is therefore not apples-to-apples.

The planner struggles to decide when to stop: no-stop oracle success (~64%) is far above SR (~26%). There is also strong overfitting to seen environments, and navigation is limited to regions covered by map nodes.
Evaluated only in simulation (iGibson) on a filtered subset of VLN-CE episodes, so results are not directly comparable to standard R2R-CE numbers.
